title: Page structure for complex sales
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: How to structure pages when buyers have many objections: an objection table, lower-commitment next steps and detail on demand.
evidence_requirements: Counter-objections from sales, support, chat canned replies or the owner
The next step options the business can offer (trial, consult, lead magnet, purchase)

decision_branches.if: Buyers not ready for a sales call

implementation_steps: Order modules by objection frequency and where each arises
Write spoiler headings and plain copy (readability test with a real reader)
Add disclosure and fallbacks (search, FAQ, chat, phone) per economics
dependencies: Mobile rendering checked (hover does not exist on touch)

cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: Page editor; ClimbOS drafts table and copy
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: Scroll/clicks on disclosures if tracked; step conversion

metrics: Clicks on primary CTA from each module
Downstream step rate (to catch deferred persuasion)
guardrails: Price, fees, cancellation and legal terms stay visible
alternatives_when_constrained: No objection data: owner's sales call notes or a recorded 7-minute pitch, transcribed
No designer: plain sections with alternating backgrounds
stop_conditions: User tests still show the top objection unanswered: move its counter higher
Downstream drop after lowering commitment: revisit the step
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Long pages fail when boring, not when long
Hidden information can conceal legally required terms

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: a page brief for any offer with 5+ coded objections includes an O/CO table and names where each counter sits

external_requirement.rule: proposed: progressive disclosure never hides price, mandatory fees, cancellation or other legally required terms

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: when a lower-commitment step is proposed, name the downstream metric that checks persuasion was not merely deferred
